A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same frequency-domain vision-token compression work, despite renaming and restructuring. Text, equations, tables, figures, and v1 Appendices A-C are readable. V3 has no separate appendices; retained appendix material can be matched to its main text.

before.justification: V1 reports original Fourier-LLaVA and Fourier-Qwen evaluations, efficiency measurements, frequency-spectrum analyses, and the model-output case study in Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains the original model and efficiency evaluations and reports additional spectrum aggregation, image-perturbation, and semantic-morphing analyses in Section 3.2.

M1.justification: The reshape, two-dimensional DCT, low-frequency cropping, inverse DCT, and flattening procedure is unchanged. V1 Algorithm 3 matches v3 Algorithm 1. Compressor placement and finetuning strategies are retained; renaming Frequency Feature Compressor to Fourier Compressor does not change the method.

E1.justification: The image-benchmark suite and MVBench coverage are retained. V3 adds diagnostic input scenarios involving pixel replacement, noise, blur, masking, and a FreeMorph semantic-transition sequence. V1's randomly generated image control is absent from the revised spectrum analysis.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MQT-LLaVA, ATP-LLaVA, PruMerge, the vanilla LLaVA/Qwen models, and the same five video-model baselines. FastV, VisionZip, and SparseVLM are newly discussed but are not added to the reported benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: V3 introduces averaging spectra over 10,000 GQA images and cosine-similarity comparisons of spatial, full-frequency, lowest-25%, and highest-25% representations under perturbations and morphing. Its spectrum illustration uses Qwen2-VL alone rather than both encoder families. Existing benchmark budgets, evaluation scripts, and tabulated training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 Section 3.2 substantially expands the investigation of frequency-band behavior through aggregate image/feature spectra, four perturbation probes, and semantic morphing. Conversely, v1 Appendix C and Figure 4, which examine caption distortions and hallucinations across compression levels without finetuning, are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new averaged spectrum is an additional descriptive analysis, not a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V3 Figures 1-3 add substantive findings about image/feature spectrum similarity and greater low-frequency stability under corruption and semantic morphing. V1's unfinetuned caption-error results are removed. The matched image, video, FLOPs, latency, and KV-cache results remain numerically unchanged; no improved benchmark performance is newly demonstrated.

T1.justification: The abstract revises the stated complexity from O(n log n) to O(n^2 log n), consistent with the two-dimensional derivation already present in v1. The illustrative dimension regime for comparing module costs is also revised. The DCT equations, FFT derivation, and overall compressor complexity remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains parameter-free frequency truncation for efficient vision-token compression, with performance retention and generalization across LLaVA, Qwen, and video tasks. The headline accuracy-retention, FLOPs, and speed claims already appear in v1. The new diagnostics principally support the existing low-frequency redundancy rationale.

C2.justification: V3 extends the existing global-structure versus fine-detail interpretation with explanations involving perturbation robustness, semantic-transition stability, and possible suppression of noisy features on RealWorldQA. It removes v1's concrete discussion of compression-induced shape/location errors and hallucinations, although the stated need for additional training remains.

D1.justification: V3 adds a repository link and retains the training hyperparameter table and compressor pseudocode in the main text. It omits v1's detailed DCT/iDCT pseudocode, explicit LAION-CC-SBU identification, training hardware and runtimes, and Qwen training pixel bounds. These are documentation changes, not evidence of altered training.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations to FastV, VisionZip, SparseVLM, FreeMorph, and the JPEG standard, and sharpens the distinction between selection, merging, and parameterized compression. The principal related-work discussion is retained; publication and title updates to existing references are not new research coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, the paper and compressor are renamed, and the architecture primer is replaced by frequency analyses. Training, complexity analysis, and experimental subsections are reorganized, with selected appendix material integrated into the main text.

P2.justification: V3 changes the two-column document to a predominantly single-column layout with a shaded abstract and redesigned headings. It rebuilds the spectrum figure, adds perturbation and morphing plots, removes the caption-error figure, and relocates retained tables and diagrams. Several tables reorder columns and abbreviate labels without changing their scores.

improvement.justification: The 10,000-image spectrum comparison and new perturbation/morphing studies strengthen the empirical motivation for low-frequency retention beyond v1's illustrative heatmaps. Integrating the training table and compressor pseudocode also improves accessibility. The gain is limited: benchmark evidence is unchanged, perturbation strengths remain unspecified, and removing the failure case and some reproducibility details weakens transparency.
